lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

To get started, could you please tell me the **name and age of your child** (or children, if you have more than one)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 10 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful to know that you have one child, Alex, who is 10 years old.

Now, to assess your eligibility, I need to understand your living situation. **Do you live with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me - they live with someone else.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with someone else, I need to understand your situation a bit better.

**Are you currently making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep** (such as money for food, clothes, pocket money, or help with accommodation costs)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards things like clothes and other bits and pieces for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. To properly assess your eligibility, I need to understand the level and consistency of your contributions.

**Approximately how much do you contribute per week or month towards Alex's upkeep?** This will help me determine if your contributions meet the required threshold for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £20 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's useful to know.

One more important question: **Has anyone else already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, or do you know if another person is currently receiving Child Benefit payments for them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 10 years old (under 16, so potentially eligible)
- Alex lives with someone else (not with you)
- You contribute £20 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child lives with someone else, you can normally get Child Benefit for **8 weeks after the child goes to live with them** if nobody else is claiming. However, **you can continue to get payments for longer if you contribute to the child's upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment rate**.

The current Child Benefit rate is £24.50 per week for the first or only child. Since you're contributing £20 per week, this is **less than the weekly Child Benefit payment** of £24.50.

This means you would only be eligible for Child Benefit for 8 weeks from when Alex first went to live with the other person. After that 8-week period, you would not be eligible unless your weekly contributions increase to at least £24.50 or more.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary:** Based on the information you've provided, you are **not eligible for ongoing Child Benefit** for Alex. However, you may have been eligible for a temporary 8-week period from when Alex first went to live with the other person (if this hasn't already passed).

If you'd like to explore your options further or if your circumstances change (such as increasing your contributions to at least £24.50 per week), you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further guidance.
